note: The fuzzer copies attacker-controlled bytes into a NUL-terminated rule buffer that is passed to the compiler.
The rule text is parsed into a regular-expression AST for a string declaration.
The AST is split into a head and remainder when a large ungreedy range-any node is present.
The loop advances using the next sibling pointer after the selected child has been detached from the AST; the safety obligation is that the traversal state must not outlive the node being destroyed.
The routine destroys the selected child after wiring the AST outputs, so any later read of that traversal state becomes a heap-use-after-free.
